intended_object: For a velocity field u on space-time, the function (x,t) ↦ u(x,t) for x in the unit ball B(0,1) ⊂ ℝ³ and 0 otherwise. It is used only inside the fixed pressure-splitting lemma of the Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák formalization. I inferred this from the docstring, the module doc and the lemma that follows it.
explanation: This is a proof device rather than a standard mathematical notion. It is the zero extension of u outside the fixed ball `pressureSplitBall` (the unit ball centred at the origin), written in product coordinates `Vec3 × ℝ` so that the library can apply Fubini and `MemLp` arguments slice by slice. The module calls this "the fixed pressure split". The body matches the docstring: `Set.indicator pressureSplitBall` applied to the slice x ↦ u(x,t) gives u(x,t) on the ball and 0 elsewhere. Its only purpose is to state and prove the slice-wise L³ bound in the next theorem, `pressureSplitVelocityExtension_slice_memLp_bound`. It packages a step of a particular proof, with a hard-coded ball and time interval, and has no standalone counterpart in the literature or in Mathlib beyond `Set.indicator` itself.
